response_text: To set up and start a thread, the user should first define the function that the thread will execute. This function typically takes no arguments and may include a continuous loop if it needs to stay active. Next, the user initializes the OS kernel using a dedicated function, which prepares the system by setting up internal memory structures such as the stack pool. Once the kernel is initialized, the user creates a thread by calling the thread creation function and passing it the address of the thread function. This lets the OS know which function the thread should run. Finally, the user starts the kernel by calling a function that triggers the execution of the first thread, causing the processor to switch to the thread’s stack and begin running the specified function from the start.\n
